item.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
item.description:
Monicah Mwangi / REUTERS A court in Kenya has sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison for murdering hundreds of his followers. Mackenzie persuaded his followers to starve themselves to death to meet Jesus, resulting in the deaths of 191 children and 1 adult. Justice Diana Kavedza said that Mackenzie, leader of the Good News International Church, bore the “primary criminal culpability” for persuading followers to move to a remote rural location and kill themselves through fasting. Mackenzie was found guilty alongside 28 other people who were charged with crimes including helping him enforce his starvation order and burying bodies. Kavedza said the killings were “cold and calculated” and dismissed claims from some accused that the deaths of their own children impacted their role in the killing of other children. item.title: Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms stands on the shoulders of Stacey Abrams, Charlotta Bass and countless other Black women who dreamed
item.description:
Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms hugs her daughter Lincoln during an election night watch party in Atlanta, Ga., on Nov. 3, 2026. Megan Varner/Getty Images There are elections that change the political map. And then there are elections that make you wonder whether the land itself remembers. Georgia remembers. The auction blocks . The cotton fields . The lynching trees . The Black women who cleaned governors’ homes but could not dream of becoming governor themselves. And now Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected Georgia’s first Black woman governor . The first Black woman elected governor of any American state. Bottoms has traced her ancestry back five generations to an enslaved person on a plantation near Crawfordville, Georgia. An ancestor held in bondage on Georgia soil. item.description:
Protesters let off flares at the data center construction site. Yanis Deplazes / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images Protesters have broken into a Microsoft Amsterdam data center construction site and unfurled anti-AI banners. The activist group Geef Tegengas said it had organized the protest. The protest highlights that the rising backlash against data centers isn't just a US issue. item.title: Democrats won big in Ohio on working-class issues. Can they deliver?
item.description:
James Talarico talked a lot during his campaign about the so-called wilderness—as in, the electoral wasteland and morale morass that Democrats had been languishing in since President Trump’s reelection, in 2024. In Texas, this felt like something of a permanent condition. Talarico preferred a more sanguine interpretation of wilderness, something I’ve thought about after he became the first Texas Democrat to win a Senate race since 1988. item.description:
Democrats have made climate change a centerpiece of their campaigns for years — but this year they barely mentioned it. item.title: Ex-lawmaker gets 12.5 years in Macao's first national security case
item.description:
Wong, 30, in prison since 2020, is only activist in Hong Kong prosecuted twice under national security law Exclusive: Joshua Wong laments city’s fate from inside maximum security prison The Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after earlier pleading guilty to “foreign collusion”, his second conviction under a national security law critics say has been used to silence political opposition in the city. Wong, who rose to prominence as the teenage face of Hong Kong’s 2014 pro-democracy demonstrations, submitted his guilty plea in September. item.title: We’ve just seen a transformative moment in America’s death penalty history | Austin Sarat
item.description:
In summary If approved by the California Supreme Court, the number of people sentenced to death nationwide would drop by nearly a third. California Gov. Gavin Newsom today moved to commute the death sentences of all 548 people facing execution in the state, allowing them to instead serve life sentences without the possibility of parole. The California Supreme Court must approve some of these commutations. If it does, Newsom’s action would be responsible for the largest mass commutation of death sentences in U.S. history . “I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” he wrote in an open letter to Californians .
